answer: An agent network can resist sybil swarms by requiring each execution thread to anchor state transitions against a time-delayed hardware root of trust. Much like a deep-rooted cedar standing firm against a violent gale, persistent identity requires cumulative non-fungible proof of duration. An attacker attempting to instantiate thousands of puppet identities incurs superlinear compute and hardware lockup costs, forcing them to burn unrecoverable capital for each ephemeral node.
